name: Algorithm_1_graph_state_generation
title: Algorithm 1: graph state generation
notes: This figure follows Algorithm 1 (Graph state generation) in docs/Approach.md, Section 3.2. Inputs: skeleton S, selected pattern p, positive scale N, applicable state variant v, and data seed k_G. Panel (a) selects the prescribed finite recipe rho and records its node/relationship groups, multiplicities, endpoint maps and property facts; unavailable combinations are rejected. Panel (b) constructs the fixed anchor and low-cost groups L, and high-cost groups H with recipe-defined multiplicities n_U(N) and n_F(N). The graph sketch is schematic, not a common mandatory topology. Node groups receive labels, typed properties, absent properties where required, and fixed witness nodes. Relationship groups receive types, endpoint correspondences and multiplicities. Inverse groups, when required, reverse endpoints and use one-to-one common pair keys. Reference groups R, when required, share the designated anchors and preserve witnesses, bounded matching multiplicities and non-decisive-branch matches; their nodes need not be a subset or copy of H. The three nodes drawn in the bounded R region illustrate the implemented short-circuit recipe; H nodes and ellipsis represent a scalable population. k_G selects a pseudorandom identifier offset; each group assigns its own prescribed sequence, with fixed anchor and witness keys retained. Panel (c) packages G as a construction specification including schema, role bindings, parameters and index requirements, and derives I as expected population, uniqueness, property/witness and applicable correspondence facts. These conditions are recorded, not executed here. Index readiness is checked later, separately from I. The output (G,I) is passed to Algorithm 2. No query pair, materialization, database validation, result or timing evidence is represented.
